GTA 6 IS OUT. HERE ARE TWO BUSINESSES YOU LAUNCH FROM ONE LAPTOP

i'm selling my TV. don't need it anymore. because the next 12 months is a window that's closing fast

GTA 6 is the biggest content event of the decade. last time a GTA dropped, kids on Shorts channels were pulling five to six figures a month off clips. this time you don't touch a single frame yourself

business 1: the clip factory

40 accounts, three agents, a mac mini in the corner of your room

→ agent 1 monitors every top-50 twitch stream. catches the exact moments chat explodes. 300+ messages a minute
→ agent 2 cuts the clip, reframes to 9:16, adds captions, generates 3 title variants
→ agent 3 pushes to tiktok, shorts, reels. rotating across every account
→ a google sheet tracks what hits. the agents repeat the format that wins

three open-source repos doing the heavy lifting:

1. yt-dlp. pulls any stream in seconds. raw material for every clip
http://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp

2. ClipsAI. detects viral moments in long video, cuts them, auto-reframes to vertical
http://github.com/ClipsAI/clipsai

3. Postiz. schedules and posts across every platform from one dashboard
http://github.com/gitroomhq/postiz

drop all 3 in one folder. one line to claude code: "yt-dlp feeds clipsai, clipsai feeds postiz, log every post in a google sheet"
zero editors. 24/7 output

business 2: NPCs that think
every FiveM RP server is fighting for the same players right now. the ones that win will have NPCs that aren't mannequins

3 NPCs running on claude. each one has its own memory and a private chat the player never sees. the tipster reads the room, the bartender works the target, the enforcer waits in the alley. you don't write a single line of dialogue

three repos that make it real:

1. generative-agents. memory stream + reflection + planning. the stanford paper that started it all
http://github.com/joonspk-research/generative-agents

2. mem0. long-term memory for every NPC. they remember your face, your money, what you did last week
http://github.com/mem0ai/mem0

3. ai-town. agents that talk to each other when you're not around. the hidden chat
http://github.com/a16z-infra/ai-town

one folder, one message to claude code: "port this to fivem lua. 3 NPCs, shared memory, one private channel"

bartenders that gossip about your crimes. cops that remember your face. gangs that plan around you

right now every RP server runs NPCs off a dialogue tree. nobody is selling ones that think yet

license it per server. 150 servers × $200 = $30K
the math

two businesses. six open-source repos. one laptop. fable 5.2 alone doesn't ship this. the repos do the heavy lifting
the kids doing this already shipped last week. the ones starting tomorrow are late

full breakdown of both pipelines, every prompt, and the google sheet template is in the article below
which one are you building first. 

the clip factory or the NPCs?

Do you think we’re living in a simulation?

This Stanford PhD raised over $300M, now valued at $2B, backed by Fei-Fei Li (@drfeifei), Andrej @karpathy, Greenoaks, & @IndexVentures, to build AI simulations of real people. 

Their Stanford research achieved 85%+ accuracy predicting human behavior.

I sat down with Simile Co-Founder & CEO Joon Sung Park (@joon_s_pk) to get into it all.

Simile (@simile_ai) builds real-world simulations with access to 40M+ real people across its global panel partnerships for companies liek Deloitte, Wealthfront, CVS & more to test major decisions.

Joon completed his Stanford PhD advised by Michael Bernstein & Percy Liang, now his co-founders, & is the first author of the 'Generative Agents' paper. That paper introduced Smallville, a simulated town where 25 LLM-powered agents lived, worked, & socialized on their own.

Recorded at Index Ventures in San Francisco, we talked about Elon Musk’s simulation theory & whether human behavior can actually be predicted..

Happy Valentine’s Day from Team Simile!

Fun fact: In our founders’ 2023 paper, @joon_s_pk and team introduced the concept of generative agents to the world by simulating a town of 25 agents… one of who was planning a Valentine’s Day party. 

The agents autonomously spread invitations to the party over the next two days, made new acquaintances, and asked each other out on dates to the party. 

This town of agents, Smallville, along with all the flirty festivities, was instrumental in creating the field of AI-based simulation. 

Love is in the air! 🎈
